title: Year four opens: four pillars
hookLine: the Catechism's four parts: creed, sacraments, life, prayer

lines: A FLOOR PLAN OF FOUR ROOMS.
cards: A thick book sits on a shelf in a parish office. Plain cover, small print, and every paragraph has its own number, so two readers on opposite sides of the world can point to the same sentence.
It's the Catechism of the Catholic Church, a summary of what the Church teaches. Open it at random and it can feel like a maze. But the book has a floor plan, and the floor plan is simple.
Four rooms. This year, called the schools of prayer and thought, starts at the front door, with that plan.

teach.b: Back on day two hundred ninety, this plan was first sketched as a map, not a wall; now, a closer look. Near its beginning, the Catechism says it builds on four pillars, following an older tradition of catechisms.
First, the Creed: what the Church believes, the faith professed at baptism. Second, the sacraments: how the Church celebrates, in the liturgy, in baptism, the Mass, confession and the rest.
Third, life in Christ: how a Christian lives, with the commandments at its heart. Fourth, prayer, with the Lord's Prayer at its center.
Believe, celebrate, live, pray. The four aren't a menu where you pick the dish you like.
When the Catechism reaches prayer, it ties them together in one breath: the mystery of faith is meant to be believed, celebrated and lived, and that living relationship with God is prayer.

teach.h: NOT A MENU: ONE FAITH, FOUR SIDES.
teach.b: One faith, four sides. The pattern has deep roots.
Acts describes the first community in Jerusalem, in the Douay-Rheims: "they were persevering in the doctrine of the apostles, and in the communication of the breaking of bread, and in prayers."
It isn't a neat match for the four parts, but it's the same instinct: faith held, celebrated, lived and prayed.
So this year takes the book part by part: the Creed first, a line at a time, then the sacraments, the moral life, and prayer. Nobody is asked to agree with all of it.
The aim is to know what the Church actually says, in its own order.

how: Catholics use the Catechism as a reference for what the Church teaches; its four parts cover the Creed, the sacraments, the moral life and prayer, and the Catechism says it follows the four pillars of the catechisms before it.

games.q: you have to lay out the whole Catholic faith in one book. how do you organize it?
o: four parts: creed, sacraments, life, prayer
games.why: the Catechism builds on four pillars: the Creed, the sacraments, life in Christ, and prayer, an older pattern of catechisms.

practice: If you have a Catechism nearby, or the Vatican's website, read the paragraph that opens each part, slowly, with a breath between: twenty-six, ten sixty-six, sixteen ninety-one, and twenty-five fifty-eight.
If not, say the four words slowly, believe, celebrate, live, pray, and notice, without fixing anything, which sits closest to your life right now and which feels furthest away.
If you pray, you can ask God's help with the one that feels furthest.
